blocks.heading: How workplace groups form
blocks.text: Formal workplace groups are deliberately created through the organisation to carry out an assigned purpose. Management identifies a task, allocates members and responsibilities and establishes reporting. Informal groups develop through repeated interaction, friendship or shared interests outside the official structure. Working near one another can create contact; trust and common interests can then sustain the group. A person can belong to a department and a friendship group at the same time. The distinction concerns how the group forms and its relationship to official organisation, not whether it is large or useful. An informal group is not automatically a trade union or an outside association.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Omi Workshop appoints a safety team. Separately, workers who travel together become friends and regularly help one another. The appointed safety team is formal. The friendship group develops informally through shared contact, even if some friends also belong to the safety team.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why fictional Oya Works’ lunchtime friendship circle is an informal group rather than automatically a trade union.

The circle develops from friendship and shared contact outside the official work structure. A trade union is an organisation representing worker interests, a different purpose and arrangement. Eating together does not by itself establish representation or union status.
